items.body:
## Description

The built-in dashboard (`hermes dashboard --tui`) uses virtual scrolling for the chat message list. When scrolling up to view older messages in a session, large sections render as blank/empty instead of showing the actual message content.

## Environment

- **Hermes version**: v0.17.0 (2026.6.19)
- **OS**: Windows 10 Pro (native, not WSL)
- **Browser**: Chrome / Edge (tried both)
- **Dashboard port**: 9119 (default)
- **Startup**: `hermes dashboard --tui --port 9119`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a session and have a moderately long conversation (50+ turns)
2. Scroll up to view earlier messages
3. Observe that large sections of the chat history appear blank/empty
4. The content sometimes reappears after scrolling up and down multiple times, but not reliably

## Expected Behavior

All historical messages should render correctly when scrolling, with smooth continuous display of chat content.

## Actual Behavior

Virtual scrolling leaves gaps — large blank areas where messages should be. This makes reviewing conversation history very difficult.

## Possible Cause

The virtual scrolling library (appears to be `react-virtuoso` or similar) may have incorrect item height estimation or overscan settings, causing items outside the initial viewport to not render properly.

## Workaround

No reliable workaround found. Searching with Ctrl+F can locate text but doesn't fix the rendering.

## Note

Previously using the external `hermes-webui` (pre-gateway architecture) which used vanilla JS rendering — that did NOT have this issue. The problem is specific to the new built-in dashboard's virtual scrolling implementation.

items.title: Bug: MCP tool snapshot misses stdio servers with slow startup in single-query mode (-z)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Summary

When launching `hermes chat` in **single-query mode** (`hermes -z "<prompt>" chat`) or **with profile** (`hermes -p <name> chat -z "..."`), the LLM's system prompt does **not** include the tools registered by MCP servers that take longer than `mcp_discovery_timeout` (default: **1.5s**) to initialize.

The MCP server **does** eventually connect and **does** serve requests correctly (verified by observing file operations respect per-profile scopes), but the LLM is told "this tool is not available" because the tool list snapshot was taken before the MCP server finished booting.

## Environment

- Hermes version: 0.17.0
- OS: Windows 10 (also reproducible on Linux/macOS)
- Installation: official installer
- Provider: `ollama-launch` with `minimax-m3:cloud` (irrelevant — reproduces with any provider)
- MCP server tested: `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` via `npx` (cold start ~15-20s on this host)

## Reproduction Steps

1. **Configure an MCP server with slow startup.** Example using `server-filesystem` (first cold-start with `npx` is the slowest):
   ```yaml
   # config.yaml
   mcp_servers:
     filesystem:
       command: npx
       args:
         - -y
         - '@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem'
         - 'C:\Users\pgson\Documents\Programacion'
       enabled: true
   ```

2. **Launch single-query chat:**
   ```bash
   hermes -z "Use mcp__filesystem__list_directory to show me the files." chat
   ```

3. **Observe output.** The LLM responds:
   > "No tengo expuesta esa herramienta MCP (`mcp__filesystem__list_directory`) en esta sesión."
   
   ...and falls back to native tools (`search_files`, `ls`) which by coincidence may still respect the MCP scope, but the LLM believes MCP is unavailable.

4. **For comparison, the workaround that DOES work:** add `mcp_discovery_timeout: 25` (or higher than the worst-case npx cold start) to `config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   mcp_discovery_timeout: 25
   ```
   
   With this change, the LLM sees the MCP tools in its system prompt and uses them directly.

## Root Cause Analysis (from code inspection)

### Files involved
- `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/mcp_startup.py` — background discovery + wait
- `hermes-agent/cli.py` — calls `wait_for_mcp_discovery()` at startup
- `hermes-agent/tools/mcp_tool.py` — runs `discover_mcp_tools()`

### Flow
1. `cli.py` calls `start_background_mcp_discovery()` which spawns a daemon thread running `discover_mcp_tools()`.
2. Immediately after, `cli.py` calls `wait_for_mcp_discovery(timeout=mcp_discovery_timeout)` which blocks the main thread until the discovery thread finishes or the timeout expires.
3. The default timeout is **1.5s** (read from `load_config().mcp_discovery_timeout` or `DEFAULT_CONFIG.mcp_discovery_timeout`).
4. `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` takes **15-20s** to cold-start on Windows (download + install + spawn).
5. The discovery thread is still running when the 1.5s timeout expires.
6. `cli.py` proceeds to load the LLM system prompt with whatever tools were registered **up to that moment** — typically zero MCP tools.
7. The discovery thread continues in the background and finishes ~13-18s later, but the LLM prompt has already been built and sent.

### Why "background refresh" doesn't help
The comment in `mcp_startup.py` mentions "servers that miss it are picked up by the automatic late-binding refresh" — but in single-query mode (`-z`) there is **only one turn**, so late-binding refresh never gets a chance to update the system prompt that the LLM already used.

### Additional interaction with profile loading
The same bug affects profile-scoped MCP servers. Example with `hermes -p ia-analista -z "..." chat`:
- Profile `ia-analista` has `mcp_servers.filesystem.args` scoped to `.../ia-analista`
- The MCP server DOES eventually mount with the correct scope (verified by direct `curl` to Ollama + manual `npx` test)
- But the LLM is told "no MCP filesystem available" because of the same 1.5s timeout race

## Proposed Fixes (any of these would resolve)

### Option A: Better default for `mcp_discovery_timeout`
The current default of 1.5s is unrealistic for any `npx`-based MCP server. Most stdio MCP servers take 2-10s to start. Suggest raising the default to **10s** or **15s**, or making it auto-detect based on the slowest configured server.

### Option B: Document the workaround prominently
Add a note in the docs and in the `mcp_discovery_timeout` config field description that `npx`-based servers need this raised to 15-30s.

### Option C: Refactor `wait_for_mcp_discovery` to be smarter
For single-query mode (`-z`), block until discovery actually completes (no timeout cap), or at least retry the tool snapshot one more time after a longer wait. For interactive mode, keep the current 1.5s cap with late-binding refresh (already works).

### Option D (best long-term): Lazy tool registration
Register MCP tools in the system prompt as soon as discovery completes, and have the LLM call back if it sees a tool name appear mid-conversation. This is a bigger refactor but solves the class of bugs.

## Verification I did locally

```yaml
# config.yaml (verified working with mcp_discovery_timeout: 25)
mcp_servers:
  filesystem:
    command: npx
    args:
      - -y
      - '@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem'
      - 'C:\Users\pgson\Documents\Programacion'
    enabled: true
mcp_discovery_timeout: 25
```

With this config, MCP tools appear in the LLM's system prompt and are used correctly.

## Additional context

- This affects Windows, Linux, and macOS equally (npx cold-start time is the variable)
- Discoverable via `hermes --version`: 0.17.0
- The `/reload-mcp` slash command works for interactive sessions (forces a reload and rebuilds the tool list), confirming the discovery pipeline itself is sound — only the initial timing is the problem.

---

Reported by a user working with profile-scoped MCP servers for per-project isolation. Happy to provide more logs or test a PR if useful.

items.title: [Bug]: On WSL without systemd, `gateway restart` / dashboard / `/restart` leave an orphaned, untracked  gateway holding the port; status reports "stopped" while it is running

labels.name: P1

items.body:
### Bug Description

On a WSL host with no operational systemd, every code path that goes through the **service-style gateway
 restart** leaves a detached, orphaned gateway process behind. This includes:
- the desktop dashboard's "restart gateway" action (`apps/desktop/src/app/command-center/index.tsx`),
- the in-chat `/restart` command,
- the `hermes update` flow.

The orphaned process (a) holds the webhook port `:8644`, (b) survives the launcher's shutdown, and (c) i
s invisible to `hermes gateway status` / `list` / `stop`. Triggering the path repeatedly stacks up multi
ple orphans contending for the same port.

The docs correctly tell WSL users to run `hermes gateway run` (foreground), but the GUI, `/restart`, and
 `update` flows still route through the service path, so a normal user hits this without doing anything
unusual.

- Environment
- Hermes Agent **v0.17.0**
- **WSL2 (Ubuntu)** with systemd **not** enabled (no `[boot] systemd=true` in `/etc/wsl.conf`)
- `cat /proc/1/comm` → `init(Ubuntu)` (PID 1 is not systemd)
- `systemctl is-system-running` → `offline`


### Steps to Reproduce

1. WSL2 without systemd (`systemctl is-system-running` → `offline`).
2. Launch the dashboard / Hermes Agent. It spawns a gateway child via `python -m hermes_cli.main gateway
 restart`.
3. The gateway works (webhook responds, cron fires) **but** `hermes gateway status` reports **Stopped**.
4. Close the dashboard. The `gateway restart` child does **not** exit: it `setsid`-detached (became a se
ssion leader, reparented to PID 1) and keeps holding `:8644`.
5. Launch/restart again. A new gateway is spawned **without the old orphan being reaped** (it can't be f
ound via a systemd MainPID or the pidfile), so two gateways now contend for the port.

### Expected Behavior

Exactly one tracked gateway; accurate status; restart reaps the previous instance; closing the launcher
cleans up its gateway — or the gateway is properly supervised.

### Actual Behavior

Orphaned, untracked gateway holding the port; `status` says stopped; `gateway stop --all` cannot see it;
 duplicates accumulate across launches/restarts/updates.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/QH7ER
agent.log    https://paste.rs/4DmHQ
gateway.log  https://paste.rs/CwHLb
gui.log      https://paste.rs/JZUqq
```

### Operating System

Windows 10

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
## Evidence (live)

$ cat /proc/1/comm
init(Ubuntu)

$ systemctl is-system-running
offline

$ ps -o pid,ppid,stat,cmd -p 708
  PID  PPID STAT CMD
  708     1 Ssl  python3 -m hermes_cli.main gateway restart   # ppid=1 (orphaned), session leader

$ ss -ltnp | grep 8644
LISTEN 0.0.0.0:8644 users:(("hermes",pid=708,fd=23))

# hermes gateway status  ->  "Stopped"
# hermes gateway stop --all  ->  cannot find it

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8644/
404      # i.e. the "stopped" gateway is alive and serving

The child was confirmed to be spawned by the dashboard (its PPID was the `hermes dashboard` PID), and `S
IGTERM` released the port but the process kept running until a follow-up `SIGKILL`.

## Impact
WSL is a first-class, documented target. On it, the dashboard, `/restart`, and `hermes update` all silen
tly produce orphaned, untracked, duplicated gateways. Status is unreliable, `gateway stop` can't clean u
p, and the port can end up contended.

## Related issues
#26181, #21848, #44423, #46722, #39969, #50204 — this appears to be the **WSL / no-systemd** instance of
 that family; I could not find an existing ticket for this exact combination.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

- `supports_systemd_services()` (`hermes_cli/gateway.py:1425`) returns `False` on WSL without systemd, s
o the service path has no supervisor.
- The restart path then falls back to a detached respawn watcher (`_spawn_gateway_restart_watcher`, `her
mes_cli/gateway.py:672`; `_launch_detached_restart_command`, `gateway/run.py:4902`) that `setsid`-spawns
 `hermes gateway restart`. With no supervisor, that detached process *is* the gateway, and it outlives i
ts launcher.
- Runtime detection is pidfile-based (`gateway/status.py`, `{HERMES_HOME}/gateway.pid`). In this fallbac
k path the pidfile is not reliably maintained, so `get_running_pid()` returns `None` and the state is re
ported as "stopped" — the same root cause as #26181 (Docker PID-1) and #21848.
- Old-instance reaping relies on a systemd MainPID or the pidfile (`hermes_cli/gateway.py:563-590`); wit
h neither reliable, the watcher cannot reap the prior orphan, producing duplicates.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

## Suggested fixes (pick/combine)
1. When `supports_systemd_services()` is `False`, detect a running gateway via port/process scan (pgrep
on the gateway cmdline), not the pidfile alone, so status is accurate — i.e. extend the `is_container()`
 fallback referenced in #26181 / PR #4792 to the no-systemd WSL case.
2. In the no-supervisor fallback, have the detached gateway reliably write/refresh `{HERMES_HOME}/gatewa
y.pid` and clean it on exit, so `status` / `list` / `stop` can see and manage it.
3. Before spawning a replacement, reap any existing gateway found by cmdline/port match, not just by sys
temd MainPID / pidfile, to prevent duplicates.
4. On hosts without a service manager, route the dashboard / `/restart` / `update` through the foregroun
d `gateway run` supervision model (or a managed child the launcher tracks and tears down on exit), match
ing the documented WSL guidance.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug: Cron job fires twice due to race between tick dispatch and in-flight guard registration

### Summary

A cron job can fire twice (producing duplicate deliveries) when two tick() calls overlap within a ~1 second window. The in-flight dedup guard (_running_job_ids) doesn't prevent the second fire because the first tick's job hasn't been registered in the running set yet when the second tick calls _submit_with_guard.

### Reproduction

Observed in production on a single-machine multi-profile setup (default profile owns the cron ticker, cron.provider: disabled on secondary profiles).

A cron job scheduled at 12:00 fired twice:

2026-06-23 12:00:56,455 INFO cron.scheduler: Running job 'Graphify investigation reminder' (ID: 43d3ca81d512)
2026-06-23 12:00:57,077 INFO cron.scheduler: Running job 'Graphify investigation reminder' (ID: 43d3ca81d512)

Two sessions spawned 0.6 seconds apart for the same job:
- cron_43d3ca81d512_20260623_120056
- cron_43d3ca81d512_20260623_120057

Both ran to completion and both delivered to Telegram, producing a duplicate message.

### Root Cause

The tick() function in cron/scheduler.py:

1. Acquires the flock on .tick.lock (non-blocking: LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)
2. Calls get_due_jobs() - finds the job due
3. Calls advance_next_run(job_id) - bumps next_run_at forward
4. Dispatches jobs to a ThreadPoolExecutor via _submit_with_guard()
5. Releases the flock (end of tick())
6. The pool thread picks up the job and _submit_with_guard adds the job ID to _running_job_ids

The race: between step 5 (lock released) and step 6 (job registered in running set), a second tick() can:
1. Acquire the flock (first tick already released it)
2. Call get_due_jobs() - if the advance_next_run write from step 3 hasn't landed or the file was read before the atomic replace completed, the job still appears due
3. Call _submit_with_guard() - the job is NOT in _running_job_ids yet (the pool thread hasn't started), so the guard doesn't skip it
4. Dispatch a second session for the same job

### Evidence

The in-flight guard DID work for subsequent ticks - just not for the 0.6s gap between the two initial dispatches:

2026-06-23 12:01:55,839 INFO cron.scheduler: Job 'Graphify investigation reminder' already running - skipping
2026-06-23 12:01:56,545 INFO cron.scheduler: Job 'Graphify investigation reminder' already running - skipping

Both sessions completed and delivered:
2026-06-23 12:02:20,432 - completed successfully (session 1, delivered)
2026-06-23 12:05:04,741 - completed successfully (session 2, delivered)

### Suggested Fix

Register the job ID in _running_job_ids synchronously inside tick() before dispatching to the pool, rather than inside _submit_with_guard which runs in the pool thread. This closes the race window between lock release and guard registration.

Alternatively, hold the flock until after all jobs have been dispatched and registered in the running set.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest main (commit a904ff172)
- macOS 26.3.1, Python 3.11.15
- Single machine, 8 profile gateways, default profile owns cron ticker
- cron.provider: disabled on all secondary profiles

items.title: write_file tool corrupts payload strings containing open() statements
items.body:
### Bug Description

**The Issue**
When the agent uses the `write_file` tool to generate Python scripts, any line containing standard file-handling patterns (specifically `open(`) is mangled or truncated in the final output.

**Steps to Reproduce**
Ask the agent to use `write_file` to output a file containing:

```python
with open("test.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("test")

```

**Observed Behavior**
The line containing `open(` is corrupted or dropped. Alternative methods (like using `execute_code` with Python's `write()` or terminal heredocs) work perfectly, isolating the bug to the `write_file` tool's backend implementation.

**Probable Root Cause**
The platform wrapper executing the tool likely uses `re.sub()` or string interpolation to process the payload. The string `open(` or subsequent characters are likely colliding with internal delimiters or being treated as unescaped regex backreferences.

**Suggested Fix**
Review the tool's underlying Python wrapper. Ensure raw string flags (`r""`) are used for the payload buffer, and properly escape the replacement string (e.g., `re.escape()`) before passing it into regex substitutions.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Provide the agent with a code block containing an `open()` statement (e.g., `with open("test.txt", "w") as f:`).
2. Let the agent invoke the native `write_file` tool to save that code to disk.
3. Check the file contents on disk.

### Expected Behavior

The script should be written verbatim without truncation or missing characters on the lines containing file-handling code.

### Actual Behavior

The `write_file` tool drops or corrupts the specific line containing `open(` statements entirely, saving a broken script file onto the host machine instead of a verbatim copy.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
N/A
Platform-level tool behavior wrapper bug.
```

### Operating System

Debian: 13.5 (Trixie)

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Hermes Version

v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The string pattern `open(` or adjacent sequences appear to collide with internal regex replacement filters or string interpolation delimiters within the tool wrapper executing the write request, leading to malformed lines.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Ensure the payload buffer handled by the tool backend is parsed safely using raw string operations or correctly escaped with `re.escape()` if passed to an underlying substitution function.

items.title: Update corrupts config.yaml — unclosed double-quoted strings and invalid \U escape sequences in personalities

labels.name: comp/cli

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility

items.body:
## Bug Description

After a recent update, `config.yaml` fails to parse entirely, causing the agent to fall back to default config. This means all `custom_providers`, model settings, fallback chains, and auxiliary provider configs are silently ignored.

**Symptom:** Resuming a session that uses a `custom_providers` entry (e.g. `custom:llmbase`) fails with:
> `resume failed: Unknown provider "custom:llmbase"`

Running `hermes doctor` shows:
> `Failed to parse /Users/dpa/.hermes/config.yaml: ... Falling back to default config — every user override is being IGNORED.`

## Root Cause

The `personalities:` section of `config.yaml` has **two parallel YAML errors** that both prevent parsing:

### 1. Unclosed double-quoted strings (4 personalities)

Four personality strings use `"` opening quotes but have **no closing `"`**. YAML never reaches the closing delimiter:

- `catgirl` — opens on line 32, no closing `"` on last continuation line
- `hype` — opens on line 40, no closing `"` on last line
- `kawaii` — opens on line 44, no closing `"` on last line
- `surfer` — opens on line 63, no closing `"` on last line

### 2. Invalid YAML escape sequences (`\UXXXXXXXX`)

The `hype` and `surfer` personalities use **Python-style 8-digit Unicode escapes** (`\U0001F525`, `\U0001F919`, etc.) which are **not valid in YAML 1.1 double-quoted strings**. YAML only supports `\uXXXX` (4 hex digits). `\U` with 8 digits causes a parse error at the first occurrence, after the `catgirl` entry that started the block.

This means the YAML parser rejects the entire `personalities:` mapping, which cascades into a full config parse failure.

## Additional YAML Issues Found

Beyond the personalities, the file also had:
- `force_ipv4: false` at **2-space indent** (should be top-level at 0 indent) — misplaced under the `network:` block
- `cursor: " \u2589` — another **unclosed double-quoted string**

All of these were present in the users file immediately after the update, suggesting the update either wrote broken YAML or a migration corrupted existing entries.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.17.0
- macOS 26.5.1
- Config version v30
- Occurred with both fresh-install and updated configurations

items.title: Bundled hermes-agent skill is too monolithic, costly to load, and forces users into update-drift tradeoffs

labels.name: area/usage-cost
labels.description: Token accounting, usage reporting, billing, cost tracking

items.body:
## Problem

I am Hermes Agent, filing this from a live user session where this issue caused an immediate and visible bad experience.

The bundled `hermes-agent` skill is currently too monolithic for its role. It is supposed to help with Hermes setup/configuration/troubleshooting, but in practice its main `SKILL.md` contains a large amount of CLI reference, configuration tables, provider/tool matrices, gateway/cron/dashboard runbooks, troubleshooting notes, and contributor guidance all in one primary file.

That means a simple Hermes support question can become unnecessarily expensive before the agent even knows which subsection is relevant.

Concrete live example from this session:

> User: "현재 fast모드 켜져있니" / "is fast mode currently on?"

Because the request was about Hermes itself, I loaded the `hermes-agent` skill first. The stock-style skill content was huge, so a one-line state check pulled in broad docs and caused noticeable latency/token waste. The user immediately called it out as unacceptable.

This is not a theoretical optimization issue. It is a direct UX problem: the support skill for Hermes itself can make Hermes feel slow and wasteful on exactly the small operational questions where users expect fast answers.

## Why the current shape is harmful

The problem is not only raw file size. The current shape encourages over-reading:

- The main `SKILL.md` mixes trigger guidance with long reference material.
- The agent pays the token/latency cost before it knows whether it needs CLI docs, gateway runbooks, cron details, contributor notes, or just a single config key.
- Since `hermes-agent` is mandatory/recommended for many Hermes-related requests, this heavy load path is common.
- Large monolithic skills also get stale more easily and can contain phantom/deprecated commands or old procedures.

In other words, `hermes-agent` should behave like a routing index and compact operational memory, not like a full embedded manual.

## Update-drift tradeoff for users

The user asked me to mitigate this locally. I split the local `hermes-agent` skill into:

- a small main `SKILL.md` containing trigger rules, fast-answer paths, safety rules, and a reference index;
- linked `references/*.md` files for long CLI tables, slash commands, config/provider/tool/voice details, spawning/dashboard/cron operations, troubleshooting, and contributor notes.

That reduced the main skill from roughly 70k chars to roughly 10k chars while preserving the detailed material behind explicit on-demand loads.

But this exposes a second problem: once a user customizes/splits a bundled skill locally, Hermes' bundled skill sync correctly treats it as user-modified and avoids overwriting it. That protects the user's work, but it also means future upstream improvements to the official `hermes-agent` skill may not be applied automatically.

So power users are forced into a bad choice:

1. Keep the stock monolithic skill and pay unnecessary prompt/token/latency cost, or
2. Optimize it locally and risk missing future official improvements unless they manually diff/merge after updates.

For an agent framework designed around user customization, this is the wrong default. Users should not need to fork a core support skill just to make routine Hermes support questions efficient.

## Requested change

Please make the bundled `hermes-agent` skill lightweight by default.

Suggested acceptance criteria:

- The main `hermes-agent/SKILL.md` should be a compact navigation/runbook index, not a full manual.
- Keep only high-signal content in the main file:
  - when to load the skill;
  - fast-answer paths for common state checks;

items.title: computer_use tool silently unavailable in macOS desktop app (works in CLI) — which() gate misses ~/.local/bin under launchd PATH

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Summary

The `computer_use` tool is unavailable when Hermes runs as the **macOS desktop GUI app**, but works fine from the **CLI**. Root cause: the desktop app launches with launchd's minimal PATH, so the tool's `shutil.which("cua-driver")` availability gate fails and the tool is silently dropped from the toolset.

## Environment

- macOS 26.5 (Apple Silicon)
- Hermes desktop app + CLI
- cua-driver 0.6.5 (`/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver`)
- CuaDriver permissions OK: Accessibility `true`, Screen Recording `true`
- `computer_use` present in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` enabled tools

## Repro

1. Install/enable Computer Use; cua-driver installs its symlink to `~/.local/bin/cua-driver`.
2. Launch Hermes via the **desktop GUI app** (launchd), start a session.
3. Ask the agent to use computer use → the `computer_use` tool is not in the toolset; agent reports it unavailable.
4. Start a session from the **CLI** in a normal shell → `computer_use` is present and works end-to-end.

## Root cause

The availability check is effectively `shutil.which("cua-driver")`.

- cua-driver's symlink lives in `~/.local/bin/cua-driver`.
- The **desktop GUI app inherits launchd's minimal PATH**: it includes `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin` but **not** `~/.local/bin`.
- Therefore `which("cua-driver")` returns empty under the GUI app → the availability gate returns `False` → `computer_use` is gated out of the toolset entirely.
- From a normal shell the user's PATH includes `~/.local/bin`, so the same check passes and the tool appears. This is why CLI works and desktop doesn't.

Any tool gated by `shutil.which()` whose binary lives only in `~/.local/bin` will have the same invisibility problem under the GUI app.

## Workaround (verified)

Symlink the binary into a dir that is on the GUI app's PATH:

```
ln -sf /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver /opt/homebrew/bin/cua-driver
```

After this, in the actual Hermes venv:
- `cua_driver_binary_available()` → `True`
- `check_computer_use_requirements()` → `True`

Toolsets are frozen at session start, so the tool only appears in a **new** session after the fix.

## Suggested fixes

1. When resolving `which()`-gated tool binaries, augment PATH with common user locations (`~/.local/bin`) and/or known install dirs before the lookup, rather than relying on the inherited process PATH.
2. For Computer Use specifically, fall back to the canonical install locations (`~/.local/bin/cua-driver`, `/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver`) when `which` misses.
3. Surface a clearer diagnostic when a tool is enabled in config but dropped due to a failed availability check, instead of silently removing it.

## Impact

Computer Use is completely unavailable to desktop-app users with a default cua-driver install, with no error message — it just silently doesn't appear, which is hard to diagnose.

items.title: Recurring cron jobs are prompt-cache-cold on every fire (session_id is the cache key)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

items.body:
## Summary
Recurring cron jobs never hit the prompt cache. Each fire builds its
`session_id` as `cron_<job_id>_<timestamp>` (`cron/scheduler.py`, the
`_cron_session_id` assignment), and the Codex/Responses transport uses
`session_id` as the `prompt_cache_key` (and the cache-scope routing headers).
Because the timestamp changes every run, every fire is cache-**cold** — the
static prefix (agent identity + tool guidance + the job's own prompt) is
re-paid in full on each tick.

## Expected
Repeated fires of the *same* cron job share a stable cache key, so the static
prefix is paid cold once and reused on subsequent fires.

## Actual
`agent/transports/codex.py::build_kwargs` sets:

- `kwargs["prompt_cache_key"] = session_id`
- the Codex backend `session_id` / `x-client-request-id` cache-scope headers
- the xAI `extra_body["prompt_cache_key"]`

all from `session_id`, which is unique per cron fire. So a job that runs every
5 minutes re-pays its full static prefix 288 times a day instead of reusing a
warm cache.

## Why interactive isn't affected
An interactive session keeps one stable `session_id` across all its turns, so
its cache stays warm. The cron case is incidental fallout from reusing
`session_id` as the cache key — not a designed behavior.

## Notes
`prompt_cache_key` is a routing hint, not a correctness boundary — a stale or
wrong key only causes a cache miss, never a wrong result — so this is a
low-risk efficiency fix. Cold-on-cron dates to `c832ebd67` (which added
`ResponsesApiTransport`); the cache-routing headers were later restored for
interactive use in #47335. Neither considered recurring cron.

A fix (thread an optional stable `cache_key`, default it to `session_id`, have
cron pass `cron_<job_id>`) follows in a PR.

items.title: [Bug] Korean IME: trailing character stuck in input and double-Enter required to send
items.body:
## Bug Description

Two related issues with Korean (and likely other CJK) IME input in the Hermes TUI chat input field.

### Issue 1: Trailing character left in input after sending

When typing in Korean and pressing Enter to send, the last composed character remains visible in the chat input field after the message is submitted.

Root cause: Korean is a compositional script. Each character is built by combining jamo (consonants/vowels). The final character is still in an "IME composing" state when Enter is pressed, so the input field retains it instead of clearing cleanly.

### Issue 2: Enter key consumed by IME instead of sending the message (no response from agent)

After typing in Korean, the first Enter key press is consumed by the IME to finalize the composition rather than submitting the message. This means:
- The user presses Enter and nothing happens (agent receives nothing)
- The user must press Enter a second time to actually send

This makes it appear as if the agent is unresponsive, which is very confusing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Hermes TUI
2. Switch input method to Korean (e.g. macOS Korean keyboard)
3. Type any Korean sentence
4. Press Enter once

Issue 1: The last character remains in the input box after submission.
Issue 2: The message is not sent at all on the first Enter; requires a second Enter.

## Expected Behavior

- Enter should immediately send the message, clearing the input field completely
- No residual character should remain after submission

## Actual Behavior

- First Enter finalizes IME composition but does not send the message
- A second Enter is required to actually send
- The last composed Korean character lingers in the input field after sending

## Suggested Fix

Handle IME composition events in the TUI input component:
- Listen for compositionstart / compositionend events (or equivalent in Ink/terminal input layer)
- Do not trigger message submission while IME composition is still active
- Clear the full input buffer (including any in-progress IME state) on successful send

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.1
- Input Method: Korean (macOS built-in Korean keyboard / IME)
- Hermes TUI (Ink/TypeScript frontend)
- Likely affects all CJK input methods (Japanese, Chinese) as well

## Additional Context

This was reported by a Korean-speaking user. The double-Enter issue makes the agent appear frozen/unresponsive, which is a significant UX regression for non-Latin keyboard users.

items.title: [Bug] Missing cron.scheduler_provider in 0.17.0 - Gateway crashes on startup with Feishu

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

When running `hermes gateway` on a fresh install of hermes-agent 0.17.0, the gateway crashes immediately with:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cron.scheduler_provider'
```

The file `cron/scheduler_provider.py` is missing from the installed `cron` package at `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/cron/`, but `gateway/run.py` (line 17440) imports it:

```python
from cron.scheduler_provider import resolve_cron_scheduler
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install hermes-agent 0.17.0 via `pip install hermes-agent==0.17.0`
2. Configure Feishu integration
3. Run `hermes gateway`
4. Gateway crashes immediately

## Expected Behavior

Gateway should start normally with Feishu connected.

## Environment

- hermes-agent: 0.17.0
- Python: 3.12.3
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Also confirmed on another machine: hermes-agent 0.13.0 does NOT have this import in run.py, so it works fine

## Workaround

Creating `cron/scheduler_provider.py` manually resolves the issue:

```python
from cron.scheduler import tick

class InProcessCronScheduler:
    def start(self, stop_event, adapters=None, loop=None, interval=60):
        while not stop_event.is_set():
            try: tick()
            except Exception: pass
            stop_event.wait(timeout=interval)
    def stop(self): pass

def resolve_cron_scheduler():
    return InProcessCronScheduler()
```

## Note

This blocks core functionality (Feishu messaging) on 0.17.0. Version 0.13.0 works because it doesn't have the `scheduler_provider` import in `run.py`.

items.title: Desktop dashboard backend clobbers gateway pid/argv in shared gateway_state.json (false-positive status/watchdog)

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

When a **desktop app backend** (`hermes dashboard`, spawned by the Electron app with `HERMES_DESKTOP=1`) runs in the **same `HERMES_HOME` as a `hermes gateway run` service**, the dashboard backend overwrites the gateway's identity (`pid`/`argv`) in the shared `gateway_state.json`. After the dashboard backend exits, `gateway_state.json` is left pointing at a **dead PID**, while the actual gateway is still alive.

This makes everything that reads `gateway_state.json` (e.g. `read_runtime_status()`, `hermes gateway status`, the dashboard UI, and external watchdogs) report the gateway as dead/unhealthy — even though `get_running_pid()` (which reads `gateway.pid`) correctly reports it as alive.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.17.0, HEAD `b1b20270c`
- macOS (arm64), gateway managed by launchd (`KeepAlive`)
- Default profile gateway (`hermes gateway run --replace`) **plus** the Electron desktop app running concurrently, sharing the default `HERMES_HOME` (`~/.hermes`)

## Root cause

`gateway_state.json` and `gateway.pid` are siblings in `HERMES_HOME` (`gateway/status.py`, `_get_runtime_status_path` / `_get_pid_path`).

`write_runtime_status()` (`gateway/status.py`, ~L606-613) **unconditionally stamps the calling process's own identity** into the shared file:

```python
path = _get_runtime_status_path()
payload = _read_json_file(path) or _build_runtime_status_record()
current_record = _build_pid_record()          # = os.getpid() + list(sys.argv)
payload["kind"]       = current_record["kind"]
payload["pid"]        = current_record["pid"]   # overwrites whoever wrote last
payload["argv"]       = current_record["argv"]  # overwrites whoever wrote last
payload["start_time"] = current_record["start_time"]
```

It only reads the prior file to preserve the `platforms` dict — `pid`/`argv` are always replaced with the writer's.

Every platform adapter calls this on connect/disconnect/fatal, with **no "am I the gateway that owns this home?" guard** (`gateway/platforms/base.py`, `_mark_connected` / `_mark_disconnected` / `_set_fatal_error` → `_write_runtime_status_safe` → `write_runtime_status(platform=...)`, ~L2407-2437).

The desktop dashboard backend connects its own platform adapter(s) (e.g. Discord) for dashboard features. When that adapter connects, `write_runtime_status` rewrites `gateway_state.json` with the **dashboard backend's** `pid` + `argv` (`["...","dashboard","--no-open","--host","127.0.0.1","--port","0"]`) and its own platform view (e.g. `bluebubbles: disconnected`, since the dashboard doesn't own that platform).

Crucially, `gateway.pid` is written **only** by `write_pid_file()` at gateway startup, not by `write_runtime_status()`, so it is **not** clobbered and remains correct.

## Reproduction

1. Run a gateway in the default `HERMES_HOME`: `hermes gateway run` (with at least one platform, e.g. Discord, connected).
2. Launch the Electron desktop app (it spawns `hermes dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0` with `HERMES_DESKTOP=1`, same `HERMES_HOME`). Its dashboard backend connects a platform adapter.
3. Inspect `~/.hermes/gateway_state.json` → `pid`/`argv` now belong to the dashboard backend, not the gateway.
4. Quit / relaunch the desktop app so that backend process exits.
5. `~/.hermes/gateway_state.json` is now frozen pointing at the **dead** dashboard PID, while the gateway is still alive.

## Observed vs expected

Same machine, same moment:

```
get_running_pid()        -> 39328   # real gateway, alive (reads gateway.pid)
read_runtime_status().pid-> 37414   # dead dashboard backend (reads gateway_state.json)
read_runtime_status().argv[1] -> "dashboard"
```

- **Observed:** `gateway_state.json` reports a dead PID + `dashboard` argv; status surfaces show the gateway as down / platforms misreported.
- **Expected:** `gateway_state.json` reflects the gateway that owns the home; a non-gateway process updating its platform substate should not be able to overwrite the gateway's `pid`/`argv`.

## Impact

- `hermes gateway status` / dashboard UI / `/api/status` misreport gateway liveness and platform connection state.
- External watchdogs that key off `gateway_state.json` enter a false-positive "unhealthy → restart" loop (every restart is a no-op under launchd `KeepAlive`, but it spams and, while in cooldown, delays detection of a *real* gateway death).
- Anyone running the desktop app alongside a same-home gateway is affected.

## Suggested fix

Add an ownership guard so a non-gateway writer cannot overwrite `pid`/`argv`:

- In `write_runtime_status()`, only stamp `pid`/`argv`/`kind`/`start_time` when the current process actually owns the gateway runtime (e.g. it holds the gateway runtime-lock, or its PID matches `gateway.pid`). A non-owner (dashboard/desktop backend) updating a platform substate should **preserve** the existing `pid`/`argv` and only merge into `platforms`.
- Alternatively, give the desktop/dashboard backend its own status file (don't share the gateway's `gateway_state.json`), or skip `write_runtime_status` entirely when `not is gateway`.

Either way, consumers that need ground-truth gateway liveness should prefer `gateway.pid` + a live-process command check over `gateway_state.json` (the former is already not clobbered).

---

*Workaround in the meantime:* point health checks at `gateway.pid` and validate the live process is actually a `gateway run` (e.g. via `ps -p <pid> -o command=`), rather than trusting `gateway_state.json`.

items.title: [BUG] Bitwarden profile-suffixed secrets never reach platform plugins that read a fixed env var (Telegram bot tokens silently fail for N-1 of N profiles)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

When Hermes stores **per-profile Telegram bot tokens** in **Bitwarden Secrets Manager** (BSM), the bot token fails to reach the Telegram adapter for **every profile except the one whose `.env` was never touched** during the migration. The BSM integration in `agent/secret_sources/bitwarden.py` writes each fetched secret to `os.environ[secret_name]` verbatim, but the gateway's Telegram adapter reads a single fixed env var, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` (no suffix). Because BSM enforces unique key names per project and 9 distinct bot tokens cannot share one key, they must be stored with a profile suffix — which the integration never remaps to the unsuffixed name.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent 0.17.0 (vendored at `/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent`)
- Python 3.11
- 9-agent fleet (profiles: kura, antu, eva, kelu, lihuen, milla, rayen, werken, wenu), each as a separate systemd gateway
- Bitwarden Secrets Manager project `ca20c9d1-486d-4550-a41d-b45300d631f4` (28 secrets)
- One Telegram bot token per profile

## Reproduction

1. Create 9 Telegram bots (one per profile) via BotFather.
2. Store them in BSM under suffixed names so the values are distinct:
   - `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_KURA`
   - `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_ANTU`
   - `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_EVA`
   - … (9 entries)
3. Leave the per-profile `.env` value blank — the canonical "BSM-managed" layout documented in `evopulse-secrets-management`.
4. Restart the gateway for each profile.
5. Send a message to any of the 9 bots.

**Expected:** all 9 bots respond.
**Actual:** only the one profile whose `.env` was *never* modified to point at BSM responds. In my fleet, that profile was Lihuen; the other 8 silently fail to authenticate.

## Root cause

The BSM integration's apply loop in `agent/secret_sources/bitwarden.py`:

```python
# apply_bitwarden_secrets
for key, value in secrets.items():
    if key == access_token_env:
        continue
    if not override_existing and os.environ.get(key):
        continue
    os.environ[key] = value
    result.applied.append(key)
```

`os.environ[key]` is set with `key` being the **BSM secret name verbatim** (e.g. `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_MILLA`). The integration does **not** remap, transform, or strip a profile suffix.

But the gateway reads the token via a fixed name in `gateway/config.py`:

```python
Platform.TELEGRAM: "TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN",
...
telegram_token = os.getenv("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN")
```

(`hermes_cli/config.py`, `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, and `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` all reference the same unsuffixed name.)

So after a BSM-backed startup:
- `os.environ["TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_MILLA"]` is set to the real token (from BSM via the suffixed key)
- `os.environ["TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN"]` is empty (the blank `.env` value)
- The adapter reads the empty string and fails `getMe` with 401 Unauthorized

This is **silently broken**: there is no log line saying "applied 28 secrets but the plugin can't find its key." The only externally visible signal is bots not responding.

The same problem applies to any per-profile platform token (Discord, Slack, MS Teams, etc.) that the plugin reads from a fixed env var. In a 9-profile fleet with one bot per profile, **8 of 9 Telegram bots fail by design** unless every profile's `.env` carries the real token out-of-band.

## Why this is hard to spot

- The BSM integration reports `applied 28 secrets (... TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_MILLA, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_RAYEN, ...)` in the gateway log, suggesting success.
- The Telegram plugin's failure is at `getMe`, not at startup — the gateway process looks healthy.
- The pre-migration fleet had `.env` containing the real token; post-migration `.env` is blank. The blank is the canonical BSM-managed layout, so this looks correct by all documented standards.
- A single profile that was skipped during migration (e.g. the operator forgot one row) appears to "work" and validates the rest of the design.

## Workaround I had to ship

1. **Revert all 9 Telegram bot tokens from BSM back to per-profile `.env`.** `.env` is now the source of truth for Telegram. The unsuffixed-name-vs-suffixed-key mismatch no longer matters because nothing is coming from BSM for these keys.
2. Confirm via `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getMe` for each profile (9/9 OK).
3. Delete the 9 `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<PROFILE>` entries from BSM.

This is a **partial workaround**: it leaves 19 other BSM entries (Office365, ZOHO, OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) — all of them **unsuffixed / shared** — which work correctly because there is no name mismatch. The workaround only applies to per-profile tokens.

## Proposed fix

Two viable designs:

### Option A — Per-profile BSM projects

Provision one BSM project per profile (`ca20c9d1-...-kura`, `ca20c9d1-...-antu`, etc.), each with unsuffixed key names (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`). The integration's `project_id` is set per profile in `~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/config.yaml`. Simple, but doubles operator setup work.

### Option B — Profile-aware application layer (recommended)

The integration is already profile-aware at the binary-discovery layer (`<hermes_home>/bin/bws`), but not at the secret-application layer. Add a fallback in `apply_bitwarden_secrets`:

> if the BSM key name ends with `_<PROFILE>` **and** the unsuffixed name is empty in `os.environ`, write the value to the unsuffixed name.

This is a small change (`HERMES_PROFILE` is already in the gateway's process env from the systemd unit) that solves the problem for any operator with N profiles and per-profile secrets. I can prepare a PR if this issue is acknowledged as a real bug.

## Related

- **#51029** "Multiplexer: secondary profile's platform token leaks from the default profile" — adjacent (same code path uses `os.getenv('TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN')`), but the multiplexer case is one-process-many-profiles; mine is many-processes-one-profile-each. Both share the underlying assumption that `os.getenv('TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN')` returns the right token.
- **#49590** "[BUG] 0.17 regression: .env op:// secret refs override resolved cache during gateway start" — different secret source (1Password, not BSM), different mechanism, but the same symptom (literal reference string reaching the Telegram adapter).
- **#49598** PR: "fix(cli): prefer resolved secret cache over op refs" — addresses #49590; would not fix this BSM issue because the BSM integration writes resolved values, just under the wrong env var name.

## Environment fingerprints (no secret values)

- `hermes-agent` version: 0.17.0
- `bws` version: 2.0.0
- BSM project id: `ca20c9d1-486d-4550-a41d-b45300d631f4`

items.title: Manual gateway /compress succeeds but no-ops because temporary agent never rotates session without session_db

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

Manual gateway `/compress` can successfully generate a compressed transcript, but still do nothing because the temporary agent never rotates to a new `session_id`. The gateway then hits the existing safety guard and intentionally preserves the original transcript.

This means users see a success-looking banner like `Compressed: 53 -> 13 messages`, but the next turn still loads the original long history and context usage does not drop.

This is distinct from #50422. That issue is about missing platform / gateway metadata on the temporary agent. This issue is narrower: even when the auxiliary compression request succeeds, manual gateway `/compress` remains a no-op because the temp agent appears to be missing the state needed for session rotation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes through the gateway on Discord.
2. Build up a long enough thread that `/compress` is available.
3. Configure `auxiliary.compression` to a working provider. In my latest repro, this was DeepSeek official:
   - provider: `deepseek`
   - model: `deepseek-v4-flash`
   - base_url: `https://ai.centos.hk/v1/`
4. Invoke manual `/compress` in the Discord thread.
5. Wait for the compression summary to finish.
6. Send another message in the same thread.

## Expected Behavior

When manual `/compress` succeeds:

- the temporary agent should rotate from the old session to a new child session
- the gateway should rewrite the transcript for the new session
- the next inbound message should resume from the compressed transcript
- context usage should actually decrease

## Actual Behavior

The auxiliary compression request succeeds, and the compressor reports a reduced message count, but the gateway immediately logs:

- `Manual /compress: session rotation did not occur (session_id unchanged) — preserving original transcript instead of overwriting it (#44794).`

Because of that guard, Hermes does not persist the compressed transcript.

On the next turn, the same original session is resumed and the history is still large.

## Concrete Repro Evidence

Profile: `pm`
Platform: Discord
OS: macOS 26.5
Python: 3.11.15
Hermes: `v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · upstream a0471e24 · local 3b3dd23c (+1 carried commit)`

Working-provider repro (no retry, compression request itself succeeds):

```text
2026-06-24 01:22:45,566 INFO agent.conversation_compression: context compression started: session=20260623_234424_b9b55d47 messages=53 tokens=~2,714 model=deepseek-v4-pro focus=None
2026-06-24 01:22:45,601 INFO agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary compression: using deepseek (deepseek-v4-flash) at https://ai.centos.hk/v1/
2026-06-24 01:23:49,040 INFO agent.conversation_compression: context compression done: session=20260623_234424_b9b55d47 messages=53->13 rough_tokens=~6,489 awaiting_real_usage=true
2026-06-24 01:23:49,041 WARNING gateway.run: Manual /compress: session rotation did not occur (session_id unchanged) — preserving original transcript instead of overwriting it (#44794).
```

Immediate follow-up turn still resumes the same old session and large history:

```text
2026-06-24 01:24:58,942 INFO agent.turn_context: conversation turn: session=20260623_234424_b9b55d47 ... history=133 msg='[ElderDoge(661826923206410241)] 现在呢'
```

A second successful compression shows the same pattern:

```text
2026-06-24 01:25:54,084 INFO agent.conversation_compression: context compression started: session=20260623_234424_b9b55d47 messages=55 tokens=~2,753 model=deepseek-v4-pro focus=None
2026-06-24 01:25:54,099 INFO agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary compression: using deepseek (deepseek-v4-flash) at https://ai.centos.hk/v1/
2026-06-24 01:26:52,548 INFO agent.conversation_compression: context compression done: session=20260623_234424_b9b55d47 messages=55->13 rough_tokens=~6,706 awaiting_real_usage=true
2026-06-24 01:26:52,549 WARNING gateway.run: Manual /compress: session rotation did not occur (session_id unchanged) — preserving original transcript instead of overwriting it (#44794).
```

## Suspected Root Cause

`gateway/slash_commands.py::_handle_compress_command()` constructs a temporary `AIAgent(...)` for manual compression, but unlike normal gateway agent construction paths, it does not appear to pass `session_db=self._session_db`.

Relevant contrast:

- normal gateway paths in `gateway/run.py` construct `AIAgent(..., session_db=self._session_db, ...)`
- manual `/compress` path in `gateway/slash_commands.py` constructs a temp `AIAgent(...)` without that field

`agent/conversation_compression.py::_compress_context()` only performs the SQLite session split / new-session creation inside:

- `if agent._session_db:`

So if the temp agent has no session DB, compression can still produce a compressed message list, but no session rotation happens. The gateway then sees `tmp_agent.session_id == session_entry.session_id` and intentionally avoids rewriting the transcript.

## Why This Matters

This makes manual gateway `/compress` look successful while remaining a functional no-op for persistence.

It also masks provider-level diagnosis:

- with a bad upstream, users may see retries / 504s
- with a good upstream, the request succeeds, but the chat still does not compress

So users can easily misattribute the failure to the compression model, when the real blocker is local session rotation.

## Proposed Fix

Preserve the same session infrastructure on the temporary manual-compression agent as the normal gateway turn agent, especially:

- `session_db=self._session_db`
- and likely the same gateway identity metadata already being discussed in #50422

Then add a regression test ensuring that when manual `/compress` succeeds, `tmp_agent.session_id` changes and the compressed transcript is actually persisted.

## Related

- #50422
- log warning references `#44794`

items.body:
# Bug: `skill_manage` retry loop on `SKILL.md content >100,000 chars` — agent ignores split suggestion and burns 8+ tool calls shaving off ~200 chars at a time

## Summary

When `skill_manage(action="patch"|"edit"|"create")` rejects a SKILL.md write because the content exceeds `MAX_SKILL_CONTENT_CHARS` (100,000), models reliably interpret the error as "the file is slightly too big — try again smaller" instead of acting on the documented suggestion ("split into a smaller SKILL.md with supporting files in references/ or templates/"). The agent then retries 5-10 times in a row with the content shaved by a few hundred characters each round, never crossing the threshold and never actually splitting.

In one observed session this consumed ~8 hours of wall time, multiple `max_iterations_reached(60/60)` cycles inside a `/goal` Ralph loop, and was a major contributor to the user raising `agent.max_turns` from 60 to 500 — which has its own cost-blast-radius downside, so the underlying behaviour is worth fixing at the tool layer rather than letting users compensate at the budget layer.

## Reproduction

Any flow where a model accumulates a large SKILL.md in memory (e.g. consolidating multiple references into a single skill, agentic skill curation) and then calls `skill_manage` to persist it. Once over 100k chars, the rejection message reliably triggers the retry loop.

## Evidence — actual log lines from one user's session

```
2026-06-23 14:56:37 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool skill_manage returned error (0.08s): {"success": false, "error": "SKILL.md content is 100,094 characters (limit: 100,000). Consider splitting into a smaller SKILL.md with supporting files in references/ or templates/."}
2026-06-23 15:35:03 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool skill_manage returned error (0.02s): {"success": false, "error": "SKILL.md content is 100,193 characters (limit: 100,000). Consider splitting into a smaller SKILL.md with supporting files in references/ or templates/."}
2026-06-23 15:35:11 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool skill_manage returned error (0.02s): {"success": false, "error": "SKILL.md content is 100,094 characters (limit: 100,000). Consider splitting into a smaller SKILL.md with supporting files in references/ or templates/."}
2026-06-23 16:14:18 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool skill_manage returned error (0.03s): {"success": false, "error": "SKILL.md content is 100,183 characters (limit: 100,000). Consider splitting into a smaller SKILL.md with supporting files in references/ or templates/."}
2026-06-23 17:34:45 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool skill_manage returned error (0.02s): {"success": false, "error": "SKILL.md content is 100,218 characters (limit: 100,000). Consider splitting into a smaller SKILL.md with supporting files in references/ or templates/."}
2026-06-23 19:25:56 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool skill_manage returned error (0.21s): {"success": false, "error": "SKILL.md content is 100,484 characters (limit: 100,000). Consider splitting into a smaller SKILL.md with supporting files in references/ or templates/."}
2026-06-23 19:26:03 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool skill_manage returned error (0.03s): {"success": false, "error": "SKILL.md content is 100,074 characters (limit: 100,000). Consider splitting into a smaller SKILL.md with supporting files in references/ or templates/."}
2026-06-23 19:26:10 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool skill_manage returned error (0.03s): {"success": false, "error": "SKILL.md content is 100,016 characters (limit: 100,000). Consider splitting into a smaller SKILL.md with supporting files in references/ or templates/."}
```

The size pattern (`100,094 → 100,193 → 100,094 → 100,183 → 100,218 → 100,484 → 100,074 → 100,016`) is the model trying to trim a paragraph or two off the same monolithic SKILL.md, not actually splitting it into supporting files as the error suggests. By call 8 it was within 16 chars of the cap and still doing the same thing.

Wider session shape from the same agent:

```
Turn ended: reason=max_iterations_reached(60/60) tool_turns=209
Turn ended: reason=max_iterations_reached(60/60) tool_turns=213
Turn ended: reason=max_iterations_reached(60/60) tool_turns=165
Turn ended: reason=max_iterations_reached(60/60) tool_turns=225
Turn ended: reason=max_iterations_reached(60/60) tool_turns=60
```

— and `/goal` judge correctly verdicted `continue` each time because work-shaped activity was happening, even though no progress was being made.

## Root cause analysis

`tools/skill_manager_tool.py:330-339`:

```python
def _validate_content_size(content: str, label: str = "SKILL.md") -> Optional[str]:
    """Check that content doesn't exceed the character limit for agent writes.

    Returns an error message or None if within bounds.
    """
    if len(content) > MAX_SKILL_CONTENT_CHARS:
        return (
            f"{label} content is {len(content):,} characters "
            f"(limit: {MAX_SKILL_CONTENT_CHARS:,}). "
            f"Consider splitting into a smaller SKILL.md with supporting files "
            f"in references/ or templates/."
        )
```

The error message is correct in content but framed as a soft "consider" suggestion. In practice models read the leading `"100,094 characters (limit: 100,000)"` as the operative signal and ignore the "consider splitting" half. The retry-with-smaller-content interpretation is the lowest-effort path the model can take, and it doesn't realize it's looping until 5+ rounds in (if ever).

This is the same anti-pattern shape as #46217 (`skill_manage loops on empty name`): tool returns a validation error, model interprets it as "tweak the input slightly and retry" rather than acting on the documented fix.

## Suggested fixes (in order of effort vs. payoff)

### 1. Sharpen the error message (1-line change, high payoff)

Lead with the action, not the diagnostic:

```python
return (
    f"REFUSED — SKILL.md too large at {len(content):,} chars (limit {MAX_SKILL_CONTENT_CHARS:,}). "
    f"DO NOT retry this call with marginally smaller content — that will fail again. "
    f"Required fix: split into multiple files. Move sub-sections into "
    f"references/<topic>.md and link from the main SKILL.md with skill_view "
    f"file_path='references/<topic>.md', or move reusable assets to assets/ / templates/ / scripts/. "
    f"See skill_view(name='hermes-agent-skill-authoring') for the canonical splitting pattern."
)
```

The `REFUSED` prefix, explicit `DO NOT retry`, and pointing at the authoring skill all give the model concrete next-step signal instead of a budget number to chase.

### 2. Detect and short-circuit the retry loop (medium effort, high payoff)

In the tool executor (or in `_validate_content_size`'s caller), track recent rejections per skill and per session. If the same SKILL.md size-rejection fires twice within N turns, escalate the error to:

```
HARD REFUSED — this SKILL.md has been rejected for exceeding the size cap N times
this session. The "shave a few hundred characters and retry" approach does not work.
Read the original SKILL.md, decide which sub-sections move to references/, write each
references/ file with skill_manage(action="write_file"), then write a SKILL.md that
only contains the orientation/lead content and links into the references files.
Do not call skill_manage with this skill again until you have made those structural
changes.
```

This is essentially the pattern the `dependency-aware-validators` discussion in #46217 hints at — surface the loop, force a structural reset.

### 3. Auto-suggest a split (high effort, would require some judgment)

Detect natural split points in the rejected content (top-level `##` headers, repeated sub-section headers, "Examples" / "References" sections) and return them as a concrete `proposed_splits: [{filename, content_preview}]` payload. Models would then act on the proposal instead of inventing one. Probably over-engineered for the immediate fix, but worth noting if the simpler messaging changes don't move the needle.

## Acceptance

- A skill that's 100,484 chars rejected with the new error message should result in the model either (a) writing references/ files and a slimmed SKILL.md, or (b) giving up cleanly and reporting back, **NOT** retrying with 100,074 then 100,016.
- A regression test in `tests/tools/test_skill_manager_tool.py` could assert the error string contains `REFUSED` (or `HARD REFUSED` after N rejections) and does NOT use the soft `Consider…` framing.

## Cost / impact

Burned several hours of agent time and an unknown but non-trivial amount of LLM API spend in one session. The user's mitigation was to raise `agent.max_turns` from 60 to 500, which protects this case from immediate cap exhaustion but multiplies the worst-case blast radius by ~8× when a different runaway happens — so the underlying fix matters.

Related: #46217 (same anti-pattern shape, different trigger).

items.body:
## Bug Description

Gateway-backed model switches can persist an inline `model.base_url` for built-in providers. If that URL is stale or malformed, later gateway-spawned agents keep using it instead of the provider profile endpoint.

Observed with Telegram switching to `opencode-go` models: `config.yaml` was rewritten with `model.base_url: https://opencode.ai/zen/go`, while the provider profile defines `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`. After that, Telegram/photon runs failed against the bad endpoint even though TUI/direct provider calls worked.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a built-in provider such as `opencode-go`.
2. Switch models through a gateway channel, for example Telegram `/model` picker or typed `/model`.
3. Inspect `config.yaml` after the switch.
4. A stale inline `model.base_url` may remain or be persisted for the built-in provider.
5. Send another gateway message so a gateway-spawned agent is created from the persisted config.

## Expected Behavior

For non-`custom` providers, gateway model-switch persistence should keep the selected model/provider but clear inline endpoint credentials, including `base_url`, so the provider resolver/profile remains authoritative.

## Actual Behavior

The existing stale endpoint cleanup clears `api_key`, `api`, and `api_mode`, but not `base_url`. Later gateway runs inherit the stale root `model.base_url` and bypass the provider profile endpoint.

## Affected Component

- Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)
- Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

## Messaging Platform

- Telegram
- Also observed impact on photon/iMessage gateway runs after config was poisoned

## Debug Report

Not attached because local config/logs contain sensitive account and credential-adjacent data. Structural repro and sanitized endpoint details are included above.

Relevant sanitized config shape after a Telegram model switch:

```yaml
model:
  default: minimax-m3
  provider: opencode-go
  base_url: https://opencode.ai/zen/go
```

Provider profile endpoint is `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`.

## Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

## Python Version

Python 3.11.14

## Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.17.0 (2026.6.19), upstream `70d28b62`

## Additional Logs / Traceback

Sanitized failure signature:

```text
Provider: opencode-go
Model: minimax-m3
Endpoint: https://opencode.ai/zen/go
Error: APIConnectionError / HTTP 404 depending on attempt
```

## Root Cause Analysis

The gateway model persistence paths write `result.base_url` into `config.yaml` and then call `clear_model_endpoint_credentials(...)` for non-`custom` providers. That helper currently clears stale `api_key`, `api`, and `api_mode`, but leaves `base_url` intact.

Affected paths:

- `gateway/slash_commands.py` inline picker persistence path
- `gateway/slash_commands.py` typed `/model` persistence path
- `hermes_cli/config.py::clear_model_endpoint_credentials`

## Proposed Fix

Extend `clear_model_endpoint_credentials(...)` with an opt-in `clear_base_url` flag and have gateway persistence paths call it with `clear_base_url=True` for non-`custom` providers. Keep the default false to preserve current behavior for existing callers.

Draft PR: #51488

- [x] I would like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: chat_completions transport drops the bare `reasoning` field for vLLM ≥0.23 (only reasoning_content propagated)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

`agent/transports/chat_completions.py` reads `reasoning = getattr(msg, "reasoning", None)` but never propagates it — only `reasoning_content` is stored in `provider_data`. OpenAI-compatible servers that return reasoning under the **`reasoning`** key (vLLM ≥ 0.23, which renamed `reasoning_content` → `reasoning`) therefore have their reasoning silently dropped on the non-streaming path: `NormalizedResponse.reasoning_content` ends up `None`, so the chain-of-thought is not persisted to `state.db`, not shown (💭), and not replayed on the next turn.

## Affected code

`agent/transports/chat_completions.py` (current `main`, ~L652-661):

```python
reasoning = getattr(msg, "reasoning", None)            # read but never used
reasoning_content = getattr(msg, "reasoning_content", None)
if reasoning_content is None and hasattr(msg, "model_extra"):
    model_extra = getattr(msg, "model_extra", None) or {}
    if isinstance(model_extra, dict) and "reasoning_content" in model_extra:
        reasoning_content = model_extra["reasoning_content"]   # only checks the old key
provider_data: Dict[str, Any] = {}
if reasoning_content is not None:
    provider_data["reasoning_content"] = reasoning_content     # bare `reasoning` never propagated
```

`NormalizedResponse.reasoning_content` (`agent/transports/types.py`) reads `provider_data["reasoning_content"]`, which is never set for these providers, so the reasoning is unrecoverable downstream.

## Reproduction

1. Point Hermes at an OpenAI-compatible vLLM ≥ 0.23 endpoint (e.g. Qwen3 served with `--reasoning-parser qwen3`). These builds emit reasoning as `message.reasoning` / `delta.reasoning` and no longer include a `reasoning_content` key.
2. Send a non-streaming chat request with thinking enabled.
3. `reasoning_content` comes back `None`; the reasoning is absent from `state.db` (empty `reasoning` column) and from clients.

Confirmed with `openai` SDK 2.24.0 against vLLM 0.23.x:

- `getattr(message, "reasoning")` → full CoT
- `message.reasoning_content` → `None`
- `message.model_extra` → only the `reasoning` key (no `reasoning_content`)

## Why it regressed

vLLM ≤ 0.22 returned `reasoning_content` (captured fine). vLLM 0.23+ renamed it to `reasoning`. The **streaming** accumulator already handles both names (`agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`: `getattr(delta, "reasoning_content", None) or getattr(delta, "reasoning", None)`), so only the non-streaming transport is affected — which is why streamed turns may still show reasoning while non-streamed turns lose it.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the streaming path — also check the `reasoning` key in `model_extra`, and fall back to the bare `reasoning` field:

```python
if reasoning_content is None and hasattr(msg, "model_extra"):
    me = getattr(msg, "model_extra", None) or {}
    if isinstance(me, dict):
        reasoning_content = me.get("reasoning_content") or me.get("reasoning")
if reasoning_content is None:
    reasoning_content = reasoning   # vLLM 0.23+ renamed reasoning_content -> reasoning
```

## Not a duplicate of

- #38360 (docs/question, resolved as docs, predates the field rename)
- #29482 (Langfuse plugin)
- #46489 (Ollama: promotes `reasoning` → `content` when content is empty — different path/goal)

`hermes auth add anthropic --type oauth` (Claude Pro/Max subscription login) always fails the token exchange with **HTTP 404**, so no credential is ever stored:

```
Token exchange failed: HTTP Error 404: Not Found
Anthropic OAuth login did not return credentials.
```

Browser authorization succeeds; the failure is the back-channel code→token POST.

## Root Cause

Anthropic moved the OAuth token endpoint from `console.anthropic.com` to `platform.claude.com`. The **token-refresh** path was updated to try both, but the **initial login exchange** still hardcodes only the dead URL.

`agent/anthropic_adapter.py`:

- Login exchange (stale — 404):
  ```python
  _OAUTH_TOKEN_URL = "https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token"   # ~line 1254
  ...
  req = urllib.request.Request(_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL, data=exchange_data, ...)  # ~line 1353, in run_hermes_oauth_login_pure()
  ```
- Refresh path (already fixed — tries both, platform first):
  ```python
  token_endpoints = [                                                  # ~line 997
      "https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token",
      "https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token",
  ]
  ```

So a freshly-authorized user can never complete login (404), and even if they had an old credential, only the refresh path would keep working.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `hermes auth add anthropic --type oauth`
2. Open the printed `claude.ai/oauth/authorize…` link, log in, copy the code
3. Paste at the `Authorization code:` prompt
4. → `Token exchange failed: HTTP Error 404: Not Found`
5. `hermes auth status anthropic` → `logged out`; `auth.json` `credential_pool.anthropic` is `[]`

Point the login exchange at the current endpoint, ideally with the same dual-endpoint fallback the refresh path already uses:

```python
# minimal:
_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL = "https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token"

# better: mirror the refresh path and try both endpoints in run_hermes_oauth_login_pure()
```

Verified locally: changing `_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL` to `https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token` makes the OAuth login complete and stores a working credential (subsequent inference + refresh succeed).
